experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep
experiences.description: Join a small-group guided jeep tour into the dark countryside away from Reykjavik's light pollution to chase the Aurora Borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts and drive to optimal viewing spots. Includes hot chocolate and photography tips to capture the lights.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in Iceland's most iconic milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. The Comfort package includes entrance, a silica mud mask, and one drink. The surreal steam-filled lagoon set against volcanic lava fields is a bucket-list hot spring experience.
experiences.best_time_of_day: Morning (to avoid peak crowds) or Evening (for aurora chance in winter)

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Relax in Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a naturally heated geothermal pool dating to 1891 surrounded by geysers and bubbling hot springs. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, it offers an authentic and affordable hot spring experience in a stunning rural setting.

experiences.name: Skyr Tasting & Icelandic Food Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore Reykjavik's culinary scene on a guided food tour sampling traditional Icelandic dishes including skyr (Icelandic yogurt), lamb soup (kjötsúpa), smoked Arctic char, rye bread baked in geothermal ground, and Brennivín schnapps. Learn about Viking food heritage from a local guide.

experiences.name: Landmannalaugar Highland Hot Springs Hike
experiences.description: Trek through Iceland's dramatic rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains in the Highlands to reach the legendary Landmannalaugar natural hot spring where a geothermal stream mixes with a cold river to create a perfect bathing temperature. One of Iceland's most breathtaking and raw geothermal experiences.
experiences.location: Landmannalaugar, Fjallabak Nature Reserve, Highland Iceland

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Iceland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Travel Day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Travel Day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and take the budget-friendly Flybus shuttle (~3,000 ISK) to Reykjavik. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort beachfront accommodation. Grab a quick snack from a nearby 24-hour petrol station convenience store (Orkan or N1) to save money on late-night dining.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In-flight meal or airport snack
meals.lunch: N/A - In-flight
meals.dinner: Convenience store snacks or instant noodles from petrol station (~800-1,200 ISK) near the hotel

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 activities begin only after 22:30 arrival. Pre-book the Flybus shuttle online for a slight discount. Keep warm layers accessible in carry-on as January temperatures average -1°C to 3°C. Download the Veður app (Icelandic Met Office) to track northern lights forecasts throughout your trip.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from travel. After a slow start, walk along the beachfront near the hotel to get your bearings. Head to the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church (free to view exterior; tower entry ~1,000 ISK) for panoramic views of Reykjavik. Stroll down Skólavörðustígur street to the city center.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the free Reykjavik City Pond (Tjörnin) and surrounding government buildings. Visit the free Reykjavik City Hall with its impressive 3D topographic map of Iceland. Walk to the old harbor area (Grandi) and browse the free Reykjavik Maritime Museum exterior. Pick up groceries at Bónus supermarket (Iceland's cheapest chain) to stock up on budget meals for the week.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Laugardalslaug, Reykjavik's largest public geothermal pool (~1,200 ISK entry). Soak in the hot pots and outdoor pools while scanning the sky for northern lights. January offers long dark nights — prime aurora viewing time. Return to hotel and check aurora forecast for late-night viewing.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered: oatmeal or cereal purchased from Bónus supermarket (~400 ISK)
meals.lunch: Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur — Iceland's famous hot dog stand, one hot dog with everything (~600 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered meal from Bónus groceries at hotel (~800-1,200 ISK). Budget tip: pasta with canned sauce is extremely affordable.

day_by_day.notes: Bónus supermarket is the most budget-friendly grocery store in Iceland (look for the pink piggy bank logo). January sunset is around 16:00-17:00, giving long evening hours for northern lights hunting. Check vedur.is for aurora activity levels (scale 1-9; anything above 3 is visible from dark areas).

day_by_day.morning: Take a self-guided free walking tour of Reykjavik's street art scene starting from the Skuggahverfi district. The city is packed with murals and graffiti art — completely free to enjoy. Visit the free Austurvöllur square and the historic Alþingi (Parliament) building exterior.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Perlan Museum (exterior free; rotating restaurant views accessible on foot nearby). Walk up Öskjuhlíð hill to Perlan for panoramic city views — free. Alternatively, take Bus Route 18 (~490 ISK single fare) to explore the Kópavogur suburb and its budget-friendly shopping at Smáralind mall.
day_by_day.evening: Northern lights hunting session: Take a free self-guided drive or walk to Grótta Lighthouse at the tip of the Seltjarnarnes peninsula (accessible by Bus 11, ~490 ISK). This dark coastal spot is one of the best free aurora viewing locations near Reykjavik. Bring thermos of hot chocolate from hotel.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered: skyr (Icelandic yogurt) with granola from Bónus (~350 ISK)
meals.lunch: Hlöllabátar sandwich shop — affordable Icelandic-style subs (~1,500-2,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered: rice and vegetable stir-fry from Bónus groceries (~900 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Grótta Lighthouse area closes to vehicles at night in some seasons but is walkable. Dress in multiple layers — windchill near the coast can make -2°C feel like -10°C. The Reykjavik City Card (~4,900 ISK for 24 hours) covers buses and some museums — evaluate if it's worth it based on your planned activities.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the famous Golden Circle — rent a budget car from Sad Cars or Geysir Car Rental (~6,000-9,000 ISK/day for a small vehicle) or join a budget group tour (~8,000-12,000 ISK). First stop: Þingvellir National Park (free entry) — walk the Almannagjá gorge between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates. Stunning and historically significant as the site of Iceland's first parliament.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Geysir geothermal area (free entry) — watch the Strokkur geyser erupt every 5-10 minutes shooting water 20-30 meters into the air. Then drive to Gullfoss waterfall (free entry) — one of Iceland's most dramatic waterfalls, especially beautiful in winter with ice formations.
day_by_day.evening: On the return drive toward Reykjavik, stop at a dark rural area to hunt for northern lights away from city light pollution. The Golden Circle route offers excellent aurora viewing spots. Return to hotel by 21:00-22:00.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered: packed sandwiches made from Bónus groceries (~400 ISK)
meals.lunch: Pack a thermos of soup and sandwiches from hotel to save money on the Golden Circle (restaurant prices at Gullfoss/Geysir are very high — ~2,500-4,000 ISK for a meal)
meals.dinner: Self-catered upon return or Subway Iceland in Reykjavik (~1,800-2,200 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Golden Circle is approximately 300km round trip from Reykjavik. Splitting a rental car among 3-4 travelers makes it very budget-friendly. Check road conditions at road.is before departing — January roads can be icy (F-roads are closed in winter). Studded tires are recommended and often standard on winter rentals.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the free Reykjavik Botanic Garden (Grasagarðurinn) in Laugardalur — serene and peaceful in winter. Walk through the surrounding Laugardalur park area. Then visit the free outdoor sculpture garden near the hotel district.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take Bus Route 1 to Hafnarfjörður (~490 ISK), a charming Viking-history town just south of Reykjavik. Explore the free Hafnarfjörður Museum exterior and the lava field park. Visit the free Hellisgerði park — a small but magical lava garden said to be home to Iceland's 'hidden people' (Huldufólk).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavik and visit Sundhöll Reykjavíkur, the oldest public pool in Iceland (~1,200 ISK entry). Soak in the hot pots while enjoying the historic architecture. After the pool, check aurora forecast and head to a dark viewing spot if activity is high (KP index 3+).

meals.breakfast: Self-catered: eggs and toast from Bónus (~450 ISK)
meals.lunch: Hafnarfjörður local bakery — fresh bread and pastries (~800-1,200 ISK)
meals.dinner: Noodle Station, Reykjavik — budget-friendly Asian noodle soup, one of the cheapest hot meals in the city (~1,500-1,800 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Noodle Station on Laugavegur is a beloved budget traveler institution in Reykjavik — arrive early as it gets crowded. Hafnarfjörður is easily accessible by Strætó bus and worth the short trip for a quieter Icelandic town experience.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Snæfellsnes Peninsula (approximately 2.5 hours from Reykjavik). Rent a car or join a budget group tour. First stop: Snæfellsjökull National Park (free entry) — the glacier volcano made famous by Jules Verne's 'Journey to the Center of the Earth.' Drive the scenic coastal road with dramatic lava fields and mountain views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Arnarstapi village — walk the free coastal path past dramatic basalt rock formations and sea arches. Continue to Djúpalónssandur black pebble beach (free) — see the ancient lifting stones used to test fishermen's strength and the haunting wreckage of a British trawler. Explore Vatnshellir lava tube cave (~2,500 ISK for guided tour — worth it in winter).
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Reykjavik as darkness falls. The Snæfellsnes Peninsula is far from city lights — an exceptional location for northern lights if aurora is active. Pull over at any safe roadside point for viewing. Return to hotel by 22:00.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered: packed breakfast from hotel before early departure (~400 ISK)
meals.lunch: Pack lunch from Bónus — sandwiches, fruit, and thermos of coffee/tea (~600 ISK). Restaurant options on Snæfellsnes are limited and expensive.
meals.dinner: Self-catered upon return or Aktu Taktu fast food chain in Reykjavik (~1,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Snæfellsnes is a full-day commitment — depart by 08:00-09:00 to maximize daylight (only about 5-6 hours in January). The peninsula road can be icy and windy — drive cautiously. This is one of Iceland's most beautiful and underrated regions, less crowded than the South Coast.

day_by_day.morning: Rest day in Reykjavik. Sleep in and enjoy a slow morning. Visit the free Reykjavik Public Library (Borgarbókasafnið) — warm, free WiFi, and a peaceful environment. Browse free exhibitions inside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Grandi harbor district — visit the free Reykjavik Street Food area and browse the Kolaportið flea market if open (weekends only, ~free entry). Walk along the harbor to see colorful fishing boats. Visit the free exterior of the Harpa Concert Hall — the glass facade is stunning, especially catching winter light.
day_by_day.evening: Self-guided northern lights tour: Rent a bike from Reykjavik Bike Tours or take Bus 11 to the Seltjarnarnes peninsula. Set up for aurora watching with a thermos of hot drink. If aurora is not active, enjoy the stargazing — Iceland's January skies are remarkably clear on calm nights.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered: skyr parfait with honey from Bónus (~400 ISK)
meals.lunch: Reykjavik Street Food at Grandi harbor — try the traditional Icelandic lamb soup (kjötsúpa) (~1,500-2,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered: homemade Icelandic lamb soup using affordable cuts from Bónus (~1,200 ISK for ingredients serving 2)

day_by_day.notes: Kolaportið flea market operates Saturday and Sunday only — check the schedule. The Harpa Concert Hall occasionally offers free lobby concerts and exhibitions — check their website for the January schedule. Today is a good day to do laundry if the hotel has facilities.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the South Coast — one of Iceland's most spectacular drives. Rent a car or take a budget group tour. First stop: Seljalandsfoss waterfall (free) — in winter the walk-behind path may be icy/closed but the waterfall itself is magical with ice formations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Skógafoss waterfall (free) — climb the 527 steps to the top for panoramic views. In winter, the waterfall often has stunning ice formations at its base. Drive onward to Reynisfjara black sand beach (free) — dramatic basalt columns, sea stacks, and powerful Atlantic waves. WARNING: Never turn your back on the ocean here — sneaker waves are deadly.
day_by_day.evening: Drive toward Vík village for dinner, then return toward Reykjavik as darkness falls. The South Coast road offers excellent northern lights viewing — pull over safely at any dark roadside area if aurora is active. Return to hotel by 22:00-23:00.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered: packed breakfast before early departure (~400 ISK)
meals.lunch: Pack lunch from Bónus — the South Coast has expensive tourist restaurants. Thermos of soup and sandwiches (~600 ISK)
meals.dinner: Sú Vík restaurant in Vík village — budget option for fish and chips or lamb (~2,500-3,000 ISK) or pack dinner from hotel

day_by_day.notes: Depart by 08:00 to maximize the limited daylight. Reynisfjara beach is one of the most dangerous tourist sites in Iceland — always respect the warning signs and never approach the waterline. January conditions can be icy on the road — check road.is. Jökulsárlón glacier lagoon is further east (4+ hours from Reykjavik) — save for a dedicated overnight trip if budget allows.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery morning after the South Coast day trip. Visit the free National Museum of Iceland (Þjóðminjasafn Íslands) — free on certain days, otherwise ~2,000 ISK. Excellent exhibits on Icelandic history from settlement to modern times.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the free Reykjavik Art Museum – Hafnarhús (check for free entry days). Explore the permanent and rotating exhibitions of Icelandic contemporary art. Walk along the Tjörnin pond and feed the ducks — a beloved Reykjavik tradition even in winter.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Vesturbæjarlaug swimming pool (~1,200 ISK) — a neighborhood pool beloved by locals. Soak in the hot pots and enjoy the community atmosphere. Check aurora forecast — if KP index is high, head to Grótta Lighthouse afterward for viewing.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered: oatmeal with dried fruit from Bónus (~350 ISK)
meals.lunch: Café Babalú — quirky budget-friendly café on Skólavörðustígur with affordable soups and sandwiches (~1,500-2,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered: baked potatoes with toppings from Bónus (~800 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum is one of Iceland's best museums for understanding the country's culture and history — highly recommended. Many Reykjavik museums offer free entry on specific days — check individual websites. Vesturbæjarlaug is less touristy than Laugardalslaug and offers a more authentic local experience.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Blue Lagoon area (budget alternative approach): Instead of the expensive Blue Lagoon (~8,000-12,000 ISK), visit the nearby Reykjanes Peninsula's free geothermal areas. Drive or take a bus toward Grindavík and explore the Reykjanes UNESCO Global Geopark. Visit the free Gunnuhver hot spring area — dramatic boiling mud pools and steam vents.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the free Reykjanesviti lighthouse — Iceland's oldest lighthouse, perched on dramatic coastal cliffs. Walk the free Valahnúkamöl coastal area with its striking basalt rock formations and powerful ocean waves. Visit the free Bridge Between Continents — a small bridge symbolically spanning the Mid-Atlantic Ridge.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavik. Optional splurge: If budget allows, book the early evening slot at the Blue Lagoon's cheapest 'Comfort' entry (~8,000 ISK including silica mud mask and one drink) — this is the trip's biggest splurge but a genuinely iconic experience. Book well in advance as it sells out months ahead.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered: packed breakfast before departure (~400 ISK)
meals.lunch: Pack lunch from Bónus — thermos of soup and sandwiches (~600 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered if Blue Lagoon splurge used budget, otherwise Aktu Taktu burger chain (~1,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: IMPORTANT: As of 2023-2024, the Reykjanes Peninsula experienced significant volcanic activity near Grindavík. Check current safety advisories at safetravel.is before visiting this area. The Blue Lagoon has reopened and closed multiple times due to eruptions — verify its operational status before booking. Gunnuhver and the coastal areas may have access restrictions.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the free Elliðaárdalur valley — a beautiful green river valley surprisingly close to central Reykjavik. Walk the free riverside trails through birch forest (stunning even in winter). Visit the free Árbær Open Air Museum exterior — a collection of historic Icelandic turf houses.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Nauthólsvík geothermal beach (~500 ISK entry in winter) — a unique artificial beach with geothermally heated seawater and a hot tub. One of Reykjavik's hidden gems where locals swim in the ocean even in January. Alternatively, explore the free Öskjuhlíð nature reserve trails.
day_by_day.evening: Final dedicated northern lights hunting evening. Take a bus or taxi to Álftanes peninsula south of Reykjavik — very dark skies close to the city. Set up with warm layers, thermos, and camera. If aurora is not active, visit Laugardalslaug for a final hot spring soak (~1,200 ISK). Celebrate the trip with a budget-friendly beer from a local convenience store (beer from stores is much cheaper than bars).

meals.breakfast: Self-catered: Icelandic pancakes (pönnukökur) made from Bónus ingredients (~500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Mandi — affordable Middle Eastern restaurant in Reykjavik, popular with budget travelers (~1,500-2,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered: celebratory meal from Bónus — Icelandic lamb chops or fish (~1,500-2,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Nauthólsvík geothermal beach is one of Reykjavik's best-kept secrets — locals love it and it's far cheaper than any spa. The beach has changing facilities and hot tubs. January is statistically one of the best months for northern lights due to long nights — if you haven't seen them yet, tonight could be the night. Keep checking vedur.is throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day — revisit favorite spots or explore anything missed. Visit the free Reykjavik Pond (Tjörnin) one last time for a peaceful morning walk. Browse the shops on Laugavegur for budget souvenirs — look for Icelandic wool (lopapeysa) at thrift stores like Rauði Krossinn (Red Cross charity shop) for significant savings over tourist shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the free Settlement Exhibition (Landnámssýningin) — an underground museum built around actual Viking Age ruins discovered beneath Reykjavik. Check for free entry days. Take a final walk along the Reykjavik waterfront from Harpa to the old harbor. Photograph the colorful corrugated iron houses of the old town.
day_by_day.evening: Final northern lights attempt — if aurora forecast is good (KP 3+), head to the darkest accessible spot. If not, enjoy a final soak at your favorite geothermal pool. Pack bags for tomorrow's departure. Treat yourself to one final Icelandic hot dog from Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur as a farewell tradition.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered: use up remaining Bónus groceries (~400 ISK)
meals.lunch: Brauð & Co bakery — excellent Icelandic sourdough and pastries, a local favorite (~1,000-1,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly for a farewell meal: Sægreifinn (The Sea Baron) — famous for lobster soup and grilled fish skewers, relatively affordable by Reykjavik standards (~2,500-3,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Rauði Krossinn (Red Cross) thrift stores are excellent for budget Icelandic wool sweaters at a fraction of retail price. Sægreifinn is a beloved Reykjavik institution near the old harbor — arrive early as it's small and popular. Tonight's aurora viewing is your last chance — prioritize it if the forecast is favorable.

day_by_day.morning: Departure day. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Take the Flybus shuttle from BSÍ bus terminal to Keflavik Airport (~3,000 ISK, departs approximately 2.5 hours before flight). Arrive at the airport with plenty of time for check-in and security. Browse the duty-free shop at Keflavik for last-minute Icelandic souvenirs — duty-free prices on Icelandic spirits (Brennivín) and chocolate are much cheaper than city shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Iceland. Reflect on 13 days of hot springs, geothermal wonders, dramatic winter landscapes, and hopefully spectacular northern lights displays.
day_by_day.evening: In transit or arrived at destination.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered: use up last hotel groceries or grab a pastry at Keflavik Airport (~600-1,000 ISK)
meals.lunch: Airport meal or in-flight (~1,500-2,500 ISK at airport)
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Budget Summary Estimate for 13 days (per person): Accommodation (shared): ~45,000-65,000 ISK | Transportation (buses + 3 car rental days split): ~25,000-35,000 ISK | Food (mix of self-catering + budget restaurants): ~30,000-40,000 ISK | Activities and entry fees: ~15,000-25,000 ISK | Total estimated: ~115,000-165,000 ISK (~$800-$1,150 USD) per person. Northern lights were best viewed on clear nights away from city lights — Grótta Lighthouse, Álftanes, and rural Golden Circle/South Coast roads offered the best opportunities. January 2027 aurora season is active — statistically excellent timing for this trip.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 22:30. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange airport transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or at airport
meals.dinner: Grab a light snack from the airport convenience store or a quick bite at the hotel upon arrival — keep it simple tonight

day_by_day.notes: January nights in Iceland are long and dark (roughly 5 hours of daylight). Temperatures typically range from -3°C to 4°C. Pack warm layers accessible in your carry-on. The drive from Keflavik to Reykjavik area takes about 45–50 minutes. Pre-book your airport transfer in advance to avoid delays at night.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from jet lag. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Take a slow morning walk along the beachfront near the resort to acclimate to Iceland's dramatic winter landscape and crisp Arctic air.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head into Reykjavik city center for orientation. Explore the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church (free exterior, small fee for tower), stroll Laugavegur shopping street, and visit the Harpa Concert Hall waterfront. Browse local shops for warm woolens and souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Join the Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep tour departing from Reykjavik. A small-group guide will drive you into the dark Icelandic countryside away from light pollution to maximize aurora viewing chances. January offers excellent aurora conditions with long dark nights.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — fuel up well for the day
meals.lunch: Café Loki near Hallgrímskirkja — try traditional Icelandic rye bread soup and skyr for an authentic mid-range meal (~3,500–5,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Grab a hearty meal before the jeep tour at Grillmarkadurinn (Grill Market) for Icelandic lamb burger or fish — mid-range option (~4,500–7,000 ISK per person)

day_by_day.notes: Northern Lights tours typically depart around 21:00–22:00 and last 3–4 hours. Aurora activity depends on solar conditions and clear skies — your guide will monitor forecasts. Dress in your warmest layers: thermal base, fleece mid-layer, waterproof outer shell, hat, gloves, and thick socks. Book the jeep tour in advance as January slots fill up.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from the late-night aurora hunt. Enjoy a slow hotel breakfast. If skies were cloudy last night, check aurora forecasts for another attempt later in the trip. Spend the late morning exploring the hotel's beachfront surroundings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa — Iceland's most iconic milky-blue geothermal pool. Book the Comfort package which includes entrance, silica mud mask, algae mask, and a drink. The warm mineral-rich waters (around 38–40°C) are perfect for January relaxation. The Blue Lagoon is conveniently located near Keflavik, about 20 minutes from the resort area.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area refreshed. Enjoy a quiet dinner near the hotel and an early night to continue adjusting to the time zone.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — take your time today
meals.lunch: Light snack before the Blue Lagoon or the Blue Lagoon Lava Restaurant inside the spa (budget ~5,000–8,000 ISK for a lagoon-side meal — a splurge worth considering)
meals.dinner: Cozy dinner at a local restaurant near the resort — try Tjöruhúsið if accessible, or a guesthouse bistro serving Icelandic fish stew (~3,500–5,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-booking the Blue Lagoon is absolutely essential — walk-ins are rarely accepted, especially in peak aurora season (January). Book the Comfort package online at least 2–3 weeks ahead. Bring a waterproof hair tie if you have long hair. The silica-rich water can dry out hair, so use the conditioner provided. Arrive with clean skin and no makeup.

day_by_day.morning: Embark on the classic Golden Circle self-drive or guided tour. Start with Þingvellir National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet. Walk through the dramatic rift valley and learn about Iceland's ancient parliament (Alþing). Sunrise is around 11:00 in January, so morning light arrives late but is beautifully golden.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle to the Geysir Geothermal Area — watch Strokkur geyser erupt every 5–10 minutes shooting water 20–30 meters into the air. Then proceed to the majestic Gullfoss waterfall, partially frozen in winter, creating a spectacular icy spectacle.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward the resort. If aurora forecasts look favorable, check the sky on the drive back — the rural Golden Circle route offers excellent dark sky conditions. Enjoy a warm dinner back in the Reykjavik/resort area.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Geysir Center cafeteria or Friðheimar Tomato Farm restaurant near Geysir (mid-range, famous for tomato soup and greenhouse dining, ~4,000–6,000 ISK — reservation recommended)
meals.dinner: Cozy dinner at Kaffi Vínyl or similar Reykjavik restaurant (~3,500–5,500 ISK) or hotel dining

day_by_day.notes: The Golden Circle is approximately 300 km round trip from Reykjavik and takes a full day. Roads in January can be icy — check road conditions at road.is before departing. If renting a car, ensure it has 4WD or winter tires. Alternatively, book a guided Golden Circle bus tour (~8,000–12,000 ISK) for a stress-free experience. Dress in full winter gear as outdoor stops are cold and windy.

day_by_day.morning: Take part in the Skyr Tasting & Icelandic Food Walking Tour in Reykjavik. Sample traditional Icelandic dishes including skyr, hákarl (fermented shark), lamb dishes, Icelandic hot dogs, and local cheeses. Learn about Viking food traditions and modern Icelandic cuisine from a knowledgeable local guide. Tours typically run 2.5–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Reykjavik's cultural gems at your own pace: visit the National Museum of Iceland (Þjóðminjasafn Íslands) to understand 1,200 years of Icelandic history (~2,000 ISK entry), or browse the Kolaportið flea market if open on weekends. Walk along the Old Harbour and visit the Reykjavik Maritime Museum.
day_by_day.evening: Second attempt at the Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep if you didn't see them on Day 2, or if you want another chance. January provides multiple opportunities with long dark nights. Alternatively, enjoy a relaxed evening at a geothermal public pool (Sundhöll or Laugardalslaug) — a beloved local ritual.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel before the food tour (you'll be eating a lot on the tour!)
meals.lunch: Included tastings on the food walking tour — you'll be well fed
meals.dinner: Matur og Drykkur for upscale Icelandic traditional cuisine (~5,000–8,000 ISK) or Sægreifinn (Sea Baron) for lobster soup and grilled fish skewers — a beloved budget-friendly local spot (~2,500–4,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Skyr food tour typically departs from a central Reykjavik meeting point — confirm exact location when booking. Wear comfortable walking shoes as you'll cover 2–3 km on foot. Public geothermal pools cost around 1,000–1,200 ISK entry and are a fantastic authentic Icelandic experience — bring a towel or rent one on-site.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the South Coast. Depart early (around 9:00) to maximize the limited daylight hours. First stop: Seljalandsfoss waterfall — one of Iceland's most magical falls where you can walk behind the curtain of water (may be icy/closed in January — check conditions). Nearby Gljúfrabúi hidden waterfall is equally spectacular.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Skógafoss waterfall for a dramatic 60-meter cascade, then drive to the black sand beach at Reynisfjara near Vík — famous for its basalt column caves, roaring Atlantic waves, and striking sea stacks (Reynisdrangar). Exercise extreme caution with sneaker waves at Reynisfjara — never turn your back to the ocean.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward the resort as darkness falls (around 16:30–17:00). Stop along the way if aurora activity is spotted. Enjoy a well-earned dinner back in the Reykjavik area.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from a Reykjavik grocery store (Bónus or Krónan) to save money, or stop at Skógafoss Visitor Center café (~2,000–3,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Íslenski Barinn (The Icelandic Bar) in Reykjavik — great for Icelandic lamb, fish, and craft beer in a cozy atmosphere (~4,000–6,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The South Coast round trip is approximately 350–400 km. Start early to make the most of Iceland's 5 hours of January daylight. Check road conditions at road.is — Route 1 (Ring Road) is generally well-maintained but can be slippery. Reynisfjara beach is extremely dangerous — stay well back from the waves and obey all warning signs. A guided South Coast tour (~10,000–15,000 ISK) is a great stress-free alternative.

day_by_day.morning: Rest day and mid-trip recharge. Sleep in, enjoy a relaxed hotel breakfast, and take a leisurely morning at the resort's beachfront. Use the morning to review photos, plan ahead, do laundry, and recharge batteries — literally and figuratively.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Reykjanes Peninsula near the resort — explore the Bridge Between Continents (a symbolic footbridge over the tectonic rift), the Gunnuhver hot spring mud pools (Iceland's largest), and the Reykjanes Lighthouse on dramatic lava cliffs. This area is geologically fascinating and very close to the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the resort. Optional: visit a local geothermal swimming pool for a soothing soak. Check aurora forecasts and step outside the hotel periodically to scan the sky — hotel beachfront locations often offer good dark sky views.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Café or bistro near the Reykjanes Peninsula attractions, or a packed lunch (~1,500–3,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Hotel restaurant at Aegean Bliss Resort for a convenient and comfortable mid-trip dinner, or order in for a relaxed evening

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjanes Peninsula is just minutes from the hotel, making this a perfect low-effort exploration day. Gunnuhver mud pools are active geothermal features — stay on marked paths and boardwalks at all times. The area around Reykjanes has seen increased volcanic activity in recent years — check local advisories before visiting. This is a great day to recharge before the second half of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) at Flúðir in the South Iceland countryside — Iceland's oldest geothermal swimming pool dating to 1891. The naturally heated pool sits amid steaming hot springs and geysers, offering a more rustic and authentic alternative to the Blue Lagoon. Surrounded by beautiful Icelandic landscape, it's magical in winter.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Secret Lagoon, explore the nearby Flúðir village and the surrounding countryside. Visit a local greenhouse or mushroom farm (the area is known for year-round greenhouse cultivation). Drive through the scenic Þórsmörk area viewpoints if road conditions permit.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavik area. Evening at leisure — explore Reykjavik's vibrant bar scene on Austurstræti, or enjoy a quiet night at the hotel. Keep an eye on aurora forecasts for a spontaneous sky-watch from the beachfront.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: The Secret Lagoon has a small café on-site for soup and snacks (~2,000–3,500 ISK), or bring your own packed lunch
meals.dinner: Snaps Bistro in Reykjavik — French-Icelandic fusion with excellent fish dishes and a warm atmosphere (~4,500–7,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Secret Lagoon is approximately 100 km from Reykjavik (about 1.5 hours drive). Book tickets online in advance at secretlagoon.is — entry is around 3,500 ISK per adult, significantly cheaper than the Blue Lagoon. The pool temperature is around 38–40°C year-round. The surrounding mini-geysers and steam vents make for incredible winter photography. Bring a waterproof bag for your camera.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Snæfellsnes Peninsula on a day trip (approximately 2–2.5 hours from Reykjavik). Visit Snæfellsjökull National Park — the glacier-capped volcano immortalized in Jules Verne's 'Journey to the Center of the Earth.' Drive the dramatic coastal road with views of fishing villages, lava fields, and sea cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue around the Snæfellsnes Peninsula: visit Arnarstapi and Hellnar coastal villages with their dramatic sea arch rock formations, the black pebble beach at Djúpalónssandur, and Kirkjufell mountain — Iceland's most photographed peak, often called the 'arrowhead mountain.' The mountain is especially dramatic against a winter sky.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the drive back toward Reykjavik as darkness falls. The long drive back offers excellent aurora-watching opportunities in rural areas. Arrive back at the resort for a late dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before the long drive
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from a Reykjavik grocery store, or stop at Fjöruhúsið café in Hellnar — a charming local café famous for fish soup with bread (~2,500–4,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Late dinner at the hotel or a nearby restaurant — Reykjavik's Grillið restaurant or a simpler option like a pizza or burger joint after the long day (~3,000–5,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Snæfellsnes is a full-day commitment — approximately 350 km round trip. Start by 8:30 to maximize daylight. Roads on the peninsula can be challenging in winter — check road.is. A guided Snæfellsnes tour is available if you prefer not to drive. Kirkjufell is best photographed from the roadside viewpoint near Grundarfjörður — the Kirkjufellsfoss waterfall in the foreground creates an iconic composition.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning at the hotel after yesterday's long drive. Enjoy a slow breakfast and a beachfront walk. Use the morning to visit the Reykjavik Art Museum (Hafnarhús) or the National Gallery of Iceland for a cultural indoor activity on a potentially cold and dark morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Reykjavik Botanic Garden (Grasagarður) — even in winter the garden has interesting frost-covered landscapes. Then visit the Perlan museum — a stunning glass-domed building offering a 360° panoramic view of Reykjavik and housing an excellent exhibition on Icelandic nature including a real ice cave tunnel.
day_by_day.evening: Third and final Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep — book this as a backup night if previous attempts were clouded out. January aurora season is at its peak, and three attempts significantly increases your chances of a sighting. Celebrate with a nightcap at a Reykjavik bar afterward.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Perlan's Café inside the museum (~3,000–5,000 ISK) with panoramic city views, or nearby Café Paris on Austurvöllur square
meals.dinner: Pre-tour dinner at Kex Hostel restaurant (open to public) — excellent Icelandic comfort food in a hip atmosphere (~3,500–5,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Perlan museum entry is approximately 4,490 ISK for adults and includes the ice cave exhibit — worth every króna. The 360° observation deck is free. Aurora forecasts can be checked at en.vedur.is (Icelandic Met Office) — look for cloud cover maps and Kp index. A Kp index of 3 or higher with clear skies gives excellent viewing chances. Keep phone charged for aurora alert apps like Aurora Forecast.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Landmannalaugar Highland Hot Springs area — note that full Landmannalaugar access requires F-roads which are closed in winter. However, the Hekla volcano area and the edges of the Highlands are accessible in January via guided super-jeep tours. Book a Landmannalaugar Highland Hot Springs Hike guided tour that operates in winter conditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the highland experience — soak in the natural geothermal hot spring pool at Landmannalaugar if accessible via super-jeep tour, surrounded by the iconic rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains dusted with snow. The contrast of colorful mountains against winter snow is absolutely surreal and unlike anywhere else on Earth.
day_by_day.evening: Return from the highlands as darkness falls. Enjoy a celebratory dinner in Reykjavik — you've earned it after a full highland adventure.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch is essential for highland tours — prepare sandwiches, snacks, and a thermos of hot coffee/tea the night before
meals.dinner: Celebration dinner at Fiskmarkaðurinn (Fish Market Restaurant) — excellent Icelandic seafood with Asian influences (~6,000–9,000 ISK) — a mid-range splurge for a special evening

day_by_day.notes: IMPORTANT: Landmannalaugar's F-roads (F208, F225) are strictly closed to all vehicles in winter. You MUST book a guided super-jeep tour with an operator who has the specialized vehicles and permits to access the area. Operators like Reykjavik Excursions or Extreme Iceland run winter Highland tours. Confirm winter availability when booking — some days the tour may not operate due to weather. This is the most adventurous day of the trip — dress in maximum warmth.

day_by_day.morning: Final full morning in Iceland — leisurely start with a hotel breakfast. Take a reflective walk along the beachfront resort, breathing in the Arctic air and soaking in the dramatic Icelandic seascape one last time. Pack non-essential items to make tomorrow's departure easier.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Reykjavik for final souvenir shopping on Laugavegur and Skólavörðustígur streets. Pick up Icelandic wool sweaters (lopapeysa), local skyr, Icelandic sea salt, birch schnapps, or volcanic jewelry. Visit the Handknitting Association of Iceland for authentic hand-knitted woolens at fair prices.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell soak at a Reykjavik geothermal public pool — Sundhöll Reykjavíkur (the oldest public pool in the city, recently renovated) for a quintessential Icelandic experience. Then enjoy a memorable farewell dinner in Reykjavik celebrating 12 incredible days in Iceland.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — enjoy it leisurely
meals.lunch: Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur — Reykjavik's famous hot dog stand, a beloved Icelandic institution since 1937 (~600–800 ISK). Order 'eina með öllu' (one with everything) for the full experience
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Austur Indíafélagið (East India Company) for excellent lamb and fish dishes in a warm cozy setting (~5,000–8,000 ISK), or Apotek Kitchen + Bar for elegant Icelandic cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Sundhöll pool entry is approximately 1,000–1,200 ISK. Bring a towel or rent one. The pool has indoor and outdoor sections — the outdoor hot pots are magical in winter with steam rising into the cold air. For souvenirs, avoid tourist trap shops and head to the Handknitting Association or Farmers Market (Farmers & Friends) for authentic Icelandic products. Budget approximately 15,000–30,000 ISK for quality souvenirs.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. If your flight departs in the afternoon or evening, use the morning for one last activity — a visit to a nearby geothermal area on the Reykjanes Peninsula (just minutes from the airport road) such as the Seltún geothermal field near Krýsuvík with its bubbling mud pools and steaming vents.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Keflavik International Airport (approximately 45–50 minutes from Reykjavik). Arrive at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for international flights. Browse the airport's duty-free shops for last-minute Icelandic spirits (Brennivín aquavit), chocolates, and skincare products. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days in the Land of Fire and Ice.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Iceland with incredible memories of aurora-lit skies, steaming hot springs, volcanic landscapes, and the warmth of Icelandic hospitality. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or grab-and-go from a nearby bakery — Sandholt Bakery in Reykjavik is excellent for pastries and coffee (~1,500–2,500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or café at Keflavik Airport (~3,000–5,000 ISK) — or use up remaining Icelandic króna on airport snacks
meals.dinner: On the plane

day_by_day.notes: Check flight departure time carefully and plan hotel checkout and drive accordingly. Most hotels offer luggage storage if you checkout early but have a late flight. Keflavik Airport has improved significantly — arrive early to enjoy the duty-free shopping and the airport's geothermal-inspired architecture. Currency exchange: use up ISK before departure as conversion back to USD/EUR loses value. The Blue Lagoon is directly on the airport road — if you didn't book it earlier, a final pre-flight soak is possible with the Premium package that includes luggage storage (book well in advance).

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Iceland Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep
experiences.description: Join a small-group guided jeep tour into the dark countryside away from Reykjavik's light pollution to chase the Aurora Borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts and drive to optimal viewing spots. Includes hot chocolate and photography tips to capture the lights.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in Iceland's most iconic milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. The Comfort package includes entrance, a silica mud mask, and one drink. The surreal steam-filled lagoon set against volcanic lava fields is a bucket-list hot spring experience.
experiences.best_time_of_day: Morning (to avoid peak crowds) or Evening (for aurora chance in winter)

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Relax in Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a naturally heated geothermal pool dating to 1891 surrounded by geysers and bubbling hot springs. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, it offers an authentic and affordable hot spring experience in a stunning rural setting.

experiences.name: Skyr Tasting & Icelandic Food Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore Reykjavik's culinary scene on a guided food tour sampling traditional Icelandic dishes including skyr (Icelandic yogurt), lamb soup (kjötsúpa), smoked Arctic char, rye bread baked in geothermal ground, and Brennivín schnapps. Learn about Viking food heritage from a local guide.

experiences.name: Landmannalaugar Highland Hot Springs Hike
experiences.description: Trek through Iceland's dramatic rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains in the Highlands to reach the legendary Landmannalaugar natural hot spring where a geothermal stream mixes with a cold river to create a perfect bathing temperature. One of Iceland's most breathtaking and raw geothermal experiences.
experiences.location: Landmannalaugar, Fjallabak Nature Reserve, Highland Iceland

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight UA arrives at 22:30. No morning activities scheduled.
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavík International Airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, unwind with a welcome drink at the hotel bar, and settle into your beachfront suite. Light late-night snack from room service.

meals.breakfast: On board flight
meals.lunch: On board flight
meals.dinner: Late-night room service at Aegean Bliss Resort – curated Icelandic cheese and charcuterie board with local craft beer or Icelandic schnapps

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Request early check-in preparation so your room is fully ready upon late arrival. Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel fatigue.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late breakfast at the resort. Orientation walk along the beachfront to acclimate to Iceland's winter atmosphere and dramatic coastal scenery. Enjoy the crisp Arctic air and dramatic ocean views directly from the resort grounds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa – Just a short luxury transfer from the resort near Keflavík, the Blue Lagoon is perfectly positioned for an afternoon soak. Book the Premium or Retreat package for private changing facilities, silica mud mask, algae mask, in-water massage, and access to the exclusive Retreat Spa lounge overlooking the milky-blue geothermal waters.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort and dine at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant. Enjoy a curated tasting menu featuring Icelandic ingredients. Afterward, step outside to scan the sky for the Northern Lights from the beachfront – January darkness offers excellent aurora potential.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic breakfast buffet at Aegean Bliss Resort – skyr, smoked salmon, rye bread, pastries, and freshly brewed coffee
meals.lunch: LAVA Restaurant at the Blue Lagoon – Iceland's only restaurant set over geothermal waters; try the langoustine soup and pan-seared Arctic char
meals.dinner: Resort signature restaurant tasting menu – expect dishes like slow-cooked lamb, pan-seared cod, and skyr panna cotta with wild crowberry coulis

day_by_day.notes: Book Blue Lagoon well in advance as slots fill quickly, especially the Retreat package. Bring a waterproof hair tie and leave jewelry at the hotel as silica-rich water can discolor metals. January sunset is around 16:00, so afternoon light will be limited.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided drive to Reykjavik (approximately 45 minutes from the resort). Begin a curated Skyr Tasting & Icelandic Food Walking Tour through Reykjavik's culinary scene. Sample traditional dishes including skyr, hákarl (fermented shark), kleinur doughnuts, smoked lamb, and local craft spirits at artisan food halls and boutique eateries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Reykjavik independently or with a private guide. Visit Hallgrímskirkja Church for panoramic city views, browse the luxury boutiques on Laugavegur street, and stop at the Harpa Concert Hall for architectural splendor. Visit the Settlement Exhibition museum for immersive Icelandic history.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep – depart Reykjavik after dark on a small-group guided jeep tour into the countryside far from city light pollution. Your expert guide will use aurora forecasting apps and local knowledge to position the group for optimal viewing. Wrap up in provided thermal gear and sip hot cocoa under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Included tastings during the Icelandic Food Walking Tour; supplement with a sit-down meal at Dill Restaurant – Iceland's Michelin-starred Nordic cuisine destination
meals.dinner: Matur og Drykkur in Reykjavik – traditional Icelandic recipes reimagined with modern elegance; try the cod head and lamb heart dishes before the evening jeep tour

day_by_day.notes: The Northern Lights Hunt typically runs 21:00–midnight. Dress in extreme cold-weather layers. Most tour operators offer a free rebooking if aurora activity is too low on the night – confirm this policy when booking. Private luxury return transfer back to the resort after the tour.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning at the resort. Enjoy a spa treatment at the resort's wellness center – opt for a volcanic stone massage or geothermal body wrap using Icelandic mineral-rich products. Relax in the resort's heated pool or hot tub overlooking the beachfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided excursion to the Reykjanes Peninsula's geothermal landscape. Explore the Bridge Between Continents (where Eurasian and North American tectonic plates meet), the Gunnuhver mud pools, and dramatic coastal lava fields. Your private guide will provide geological and cultural context throughout.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a private in-suite dining experience. Arrange with the concierge for a chef to prepare a bespoke Icelandic dinner in your suite – fresh langoustine, Icelandic lamb rack, and a selection of local cheeses paired with Icelandic wines and craft beers.

meals.breakfast: À la carte breakfast at the resort – smoked salmon eggs Benedict with Icelandic rye bread
meals.lunch: Picnic-style gourmet lunch box prepared by the resort chef, enjoyed at a scenic viewpoint on the Reykjanes Peninsula
meals.dinner: Private in-suite chef's dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjanes Peninsula is highly geologically active – check for any volcanic or geothermal access restrictions before the excursion. The area has seen increased volcanic activity in recent years, so your guide will have the latest safety information.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure for a full-day premium Golden Circle tour via private luxury vehicle with a dedicated guide. First stop: Þingvellir National Park – a UNESCO World Heritage Site where you can walk between the tectonic plates and explore the ancient Viking parliament site. In winter, the park is hauntingly beautiful with frost and low golden light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle to the Geysir Geothermal Area to witness Strokkur geyser erupt every 5–10 minutes. Then proceed to the majestic Gullfoss waterfall, partially frozen in January, creating an extraordinary icy spectacle. Your private guide will secure exclusive viewpoints away from any crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak in Flúðir – end the Golden Circle day with a relaxing soak in Iceland's oldest swimming pool, dating to 1891. The naturally heated geothermal pool is surrounded by geysers and hot springs, and in January the contrast of warm water against cold air and possible aurora overhead is magical. Private evening booking recommended.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast – hearty Icelandic oatmeal with wild berries, skyr, and smoked meats
meals.lunch: Lindin Restaurant in Laugarvatn – one of Iceland's finest regional restaurants on the shores of Lake Laugarvatn; known for geothermally baked bread and fresh lake fish
meals.dinner: Efstadalur II Farm Restaurant near Gullfoss – a charming farm-to-table restaurant with homemade ice cream, lamb, and locally sourced produce; cozy fireplace atmosphere

day_by_day.notes: The Golden Circle is approximately a 300 km loop from Reykjavik. With a private vehicle and guide, you can take your time without rushing. January road conditions may require a 4WD vehicle – ensure your private transfer uses a suitable vehicle. Return to resort late evening.

day_by_day.morning: Full leisure morning at the resort. Sleep in and enjoy a long, indulgent breakfast. Book a private yoga or meditation session through the resort's wellness program, ideally in a glass-walled studio overlooking the ocean for a serene Arctic experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Landmannalaugar Highland Hot Springs Hike – embark on a guided excursion to Iceland's dramatic Highlands (note: full Landmannalaugar access may be limited in deep winter; confirm with your guide for the January-accessible version of this experience, which may involve a modified route through the rhyolite mountains). Trek through rainbow-colored mountains to reach natural geothermal hot spring pools for an unforgettable soak in the wilderness.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Enjoy a premium spa evening – book the resort's signature couple's or solo thermal circuit including steam room, ice plunge, and relaxation lounge. Conclude with a light, health-focused dinner at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely full breakfast at the resort – freshly baked pastries, Icelandic pancakes with bilberry jam, and a Bloody Mary with Icelandic vodka
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch provided by the resort or guide service for the Highland excursion – thermos of lamb soup, artisan sandwiches, and hot chocolate
meals.dinner: Resort health-focused dinner – pan-seared Arctic char with dill cream, roasted root vegetables, and skyr mousse with wild blueberries

day_by_day.notes: Landmannalaugar is typically only accessible by super-jeep in winter and some routes may be closed due to snow. Always confirm accessibility with a specialized Highland tour operator before booking. This is a strenuous hike even in summer – ensure appropriate fitness and gear.

day_by_day.morning: Private half-day excursion to the Snæfellsnes Peninsula (approximately 2.5 hours from the resort). Begin with a visit to the iconic Snæfellsjökull glacier volcano – immortalized in Jules Verne's 'Journey to the Center of the Earth.' Explore the dramatic black lava coastline and the charming fishing village of Arnarstapi.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the Snæfellsnes Peninsula to Kirkjufell mountain – one of Iceland's most photographed peaks – and the adjacent Kirkjufellsfoss waterfall. In January, the landscape is blanketed in snow and ice, creating an extraordinary winter tableau. Your guide will position you for the best photography angles.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey toward the resort. Stop for dinner in Borgarnes or Akranes en route. Arrive back at the resort by late evening. Check aurora forecast and consider a spontaneous Northern Lights viewing session from the beachfront if conditions are favorable.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast – eggs your way with Icelandic smoked salmon and rye toast
meals.lunch: Bjarnarhöfn Shark Museum Café in Snæfellsnes – sample hákarl (fermented Greenlandic shark) paired with Brennivín schnapps for an authentic cultural experience
meals.dinner: Hyrnan Restaurant in Borgarnes – known for excellent lamb and fresh fish in a cozy setting; try the slow-braised Icelandic lamb shank

day_by_day.notes: The Snæfellsnes Peninsula is a full-day excursion and may require an overnight stay if you wish to explore more thoroughly. For a day trip, depart no later than 08:00. Road conditions in January can be challenging – private 4WD transfer is essential.

day_by_day.morning: Rest day at the resort. Enjoy a private photography workshop with an Icelandic landscape photographer – learn to capture the unique winter light, long exposure techniques for aurora photography, and composition in Iceland's dramatic scenery, all from the resort's stunning beachfront location.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return visit to the Blue Lagoon for a second, more relaxed experience – this time book the exclusive Retreat Spa for a full afternoon of thermal bathing, private lagoon access, in-water floating therapy, and the signature Sky Lagoon ritual. The Retreat offers an unmatched level of privacy and luxury.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset (around 16:00) cocktails at the resort's oceanfront bar. Enjoy Icelandic craft gin and tonics or a Brennivín-based cocktail as the sky transitions from twilight to deep Arctic darkness. Dine at the resort's fine dining restaurant with a focus on the chef's seasonal tasting menu.

meals.breakfast: Room service breakfast in bed – full Icelandic spread with freshly squeezed cloudberry juice
meals.lunch: The Retreat at Blue Lagoon Restaurant – elegant Nordic cuisine with panoramic lagoon views; try the smoked lamb tartare and Arctic char crudo
meals.dinner: Resort signature tasting menu – seven-course chef's seasonal menu with wine pairing featuring Icelandic ingredients and Nordic culinary techniques

day_by_day.notes: The Retreat at Blue Lagoon is the most exclusive and expensive tier of the Blue Lagoon experience – book months in advance. Minimum age is 18. This is an ideal day for pure luxury indulgence and relaxation mid-trip.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided excursion to the South Coast of Iceland. Depart early to maximize the limited daylight hours. First stop: Seljalandsfoss waterfall – a dramatic cascade you can walk behind (may be icy in January; your guide will assess safety). Then visit the hidden Gljúfrabúi waterfall tucked inside a canyon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Skógafoss waterfall for its iconic rainbow mist (even in winter). Explore the black sand beaches of Reynisfjara – one of the world's most dramatic beaches with towering basalt columns and powerful Atlantic waves. Visit the nearby Reynisdrangar sea stacks. Continue to the town of Vík for a brief exploration.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a pre-arranged luxury overnight accommodation near Vík (such as Hotel Katla by Keahotels or a premium guesthouse) for a two-night South Coast extension, or return to the resort via private transfer. If staying, enjoy a candlelit dinner at the hotel restaurant and aurora watch from the countryside.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast – protein-rich smoked lamb and eggs before the long excursion day
meals.lunch: Skál! Restaurant in Vík – known for fresh fish soup, lamb burgers, and hearty Icelandic comfort food in a cozy setting
meals.dinner: Hotel Katla Restaurant (if staying overnight) or resort dinner upon return – slow-roasted lamb with root vegetable purée and Icelandic wild herb sauce

day_by_day.notes: The South Coast is approximately 2–2.5 hours from the resort. This is a long but highly rewarding day. Reynisfjara beach has extremely dangerous sneaker waves – never turn your back on the ocean and always stay behind the safety markers. January road conditions require 4WD.

day_by_day.morning: If on South Coast extension: Morning visit to Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon – one of Iceland's most spectacular sights, where enormous icebergs calve from Breiðamerkurjökull glacier into a stunning lagoon. In January, the lagoon may be partially frozen, creating an otherworldly icy landscape. Walk to nearby Diamond Beach where ice chunks wash ashore on black sand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Vatnajökull National Park visitor center for context on Europe's largest glacier. Optional glacier walk or ice cave tour with a certified guide (January is prime season for ice cave tours inside Vatnajökull – the crystal blue ice caves are at their most stable and spectacular in midwinter). This is a bucket-list experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort (approximately 4–5 hours from the glacier lagoon). Arrive late evening and enjoy a restorative room service dinner and early night to recover from two days of South Coast exploration.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at South Coast accommodation or packed resort-prepared breakfast box
meals.lunch: Glacier Goose Restaurant near Jökulsárlón – simple but satisfying glacier lagoon views with lamb soup and fresh sandwiches
meals.dinner: Room service at Aegean Bliss Resort upon return – comforting Icelandic lamb stew with fresh bread and a glass of Icelandic birch schnapps

day_by_day.notes: Ice cave tours inside Vatnajökull must be booked well in advance with certified glacier guides only. Never enter ice caves without a guide. The caves change each season and some years are more accessible than others. January 2027 cave availability should be confirmed with local operators such as Local Guide or Glacier Guides.

day_by_day.morning: Full resort spa day. Begin with a 90-minute volcanic hot stone massage followed by a geothermal facial using Icelandic mineral products. Spend time in the resort's thermal facilities – steam room, sauna, cold plunge pool, and relaxation lounge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private cooking class at the resort or at a Reykjavik culinary studio. Learn to prepare traditional Icelandic dishes with a professional chef – including skyr-marinated lamb, geothermally baked rye bread (hverabrauð), and traditional Icelandic fish stew (plokkfiskur). Take home the recipes as a lasting memory.
day_by_day.evening: Final Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep – book a second attempt on a different route for the best possible aurora viewing opportunity. Your guide will have updated forecasts and will venture to the darkest, most remote locations. This is your last dedicated aurora hunting night.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast – slow morning with fresh-baked pastries, skyr parfait, and Icelandic herbal tea
meals.lunch: Light spa lunch at the resort wellness café – smoked salmon avocado toast, green smoothies, and Icelandic mineral water
meals.dinner: Post-Northern Lights late dinner at the resort bar – Icelandic lamb sliders, truffle fries, and a local craft beer nightcap

day_by_day.notes: January aurora forecasts in Iceland can be checked via the Icelandic Meteorological Office app (Vedur) and the Aurora Forecast app. Cloud cover is the primary obstacle – your jeep guide will drive to areas with clear skies if needed. KP index of 3 or above with clear skies gives excellent viewing odds.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to the lesser-known Krauma Geothermal Baths near Reykholt in West Iceland (approximately 1.5 hours from the resort). Krauma is fed by Europe's most powerful hot spring, Deildartunguhver, and offers a more intimate and exclusive alternative to the Blue Lagoon with five natural baths of varying temperatures and a cold plunge pool.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the historic Reykholt area – visit the medieval home of Snorri Sturluson, the famous 13th-century Icelandic poet and historian. Tour the Snorralaug hot spring pool (one of Iceland's oldest man-made structures) and the Snorrastofa cultural center for a deep dive into Norse and Icelandic saga culture.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a farewell dinner. Request a private table on the beachfront terrace (weather permitting) or in a secluded corner of the resort's finest restaurant. Celebrate the journey with a premium wine pairing dinner and a toast with Icelandic Brennivín or a glass of Champagne.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast – smoked lamb hash with poached eggs and hollandaise, fresh juice, and Icelandic coffee
meals.lunch: Krauma Café at the geothermal baths – light lunch of Icelandic lamb soup, fresh bread, and herbal tea in a cozy post-soak setting
meals.dinner: Farewell tasting dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort's signature restaurant – premium eight-course menu with Icelandic langoustine, dry-aged lamb, and a skyr soufflé dessert with full wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Krauma Geothermal Baths is a hidden gem that offers a far more intimate experience than the Blue Lagoon with a fraction of the visitors. Book in advance. The drive through West Iceland's Borgarfjörður valley is scenic even in winter. This is a perfect penultimate day combining culture, wellness, and fine dining.

day_by_day.morning: Final leisurely morning at Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy one last full Icelandic breakfast at the resort. Take a slow beachfront walk to collect final memories of Iceland's dramatic winter coastline. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Late checkout (arrange with concierge in advance for a 14:00 or later checkout). Spend remaining time in the resort's thermal pool or hot tub, or enjoy a final spa treatment. Private luxury transfer to Keflavík International Airport departs in the early-to-mid afternoon depending on your outbound flight time.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Keflavík International Airport. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of geothermal wonders, Northern Lights, culinary adventures, and Iceland's breathtaking winter landscapes.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the resort – order everything you haven't yet tried: Icelandic crepes with crowberry jam, smoked whale (if desired), skyr with honey, and a final cup of Icelandic coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort or airport lounge – Icelandic smoked salmon wrap and a Skyr smoothie
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or on-board flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Keflavík Airport is approximately 45–50 minutes from the resort. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for check-in and security. Purchase last-minute Icelandic souvenirs at the airport duty-free – Icelandic wool sweaters (lopapeysa), lava salt, skyr products, and Brennivín schnapps make excellent gifts. Confirm late checkout with the resort at least 48 hours in advance.

query: Iceland Northern Lights and hot springs, $3500 couple, January 2026
